faq.title: Why is using a keyboard app without internet permission considered critical for security?
faq.description: Your virtual keyboard is the single most sensitive software component on your smartphone. Every password you type, bank account number you enter, two-factor OTP you paste, and confidential message you draft passes directly through the keyboard input method editor (IME). If a keyboard possesses the `android.permission.INTERNET` permission (like Gboard or SwiftKey), it has the technical capability to transmit your keystrokes to remote servers for telemetry or advertising analytics.

faq.title: Can an open-source keyboard support swipe gesture typing without sending data to Google?
faq.description: Yes! Modern open-source keyboards like HeliBoard support full glide/swipe typing offline. By importing an offline gesture typing binary library (`libjni_latinimegoogle.so`), HeliBoard calculates swipe gestures locally on your smartphone's CPU with zero network communication.

faq.title: How does FUTO Keyboard perform voice typing without connecting to cloud voice servers?
faq.description: Traditional voice typing (Google Voice / Siri) streams your audio recordings to corporate cloud datacenters for transcription. FUTO Keyboard downloads a compact, quantized neural voice recognition model (OpenAI Whisper) directly to your smartphone's internal storage, running voice-to-text inference entirely on your phone's local NPU/CPU.

html:
The Most Dangerous App on Your Smartphone

When users consider smartphone security, they worry about malicious PDF attachments, fraudulent banking links, or rogue camera permissions. Yet few stop to examine the application that records their most intimate thoughts, confidential passwords, and financial secrets: their virtual keyboard.

By default, 90% of Android devices ship with either Google Gboard or Microsoft SwiftKey preinstalled. While these keyboards offer fluid auto-correction and cloud sync, they operate under an alarming technical reality: they possess the android.permission.INTERNET permission. Under the guise of 'Personalized Dictionaries', 'Predictive Text Suggestions', and 'Diagnostic Feedback', these keyboards maintain continuous socket connections to corporate cloud servers, uploading telemetry and linguistic models. If you type medical symptoms into a browser or discuss sensitive business strategies in an encrypted chat like Signal, your keyboard's predictive algorithms index those words.

The definitive solution is simple: use a keyboard that does not even possess the code to access the internet. In Android's permission model, an app that does not declare network permissions in its manifest cannot connect to the web under any circumstances. This comprehensive guide reviews the top open-source Android keyboards that deliver modern swipe typing, voice input, and themes with 100% offline security.

Why Open-Source Keyboard Architecture Matters

Switching to an open-source keyboard provides three non-negotiable security benefits:

  1. Mathematically Enforced Privacy: In keyboards like HeliBoard and FlorisBoard, the INTERNET permission is omitted from the AndroidManifest.xml. Even if a rogue update were pushed, the Android operating system kernel physically blocks the app from opening network sockets.
  2. Auditable Codebase: Open-source projects host their complete source code on platforms like GitHub and Codeberg. Thousands of independent security engineers inspect the code to ensure zero hidden keyloggers or telemetry backdoors exist.
  3. Immunity to Corporate Monetization: Commercial keyboards frequently introduce sponsored stickers, AI search bars, and trending GIF tabs to monetize user data. Open-source keyboards remain clean, lightweight, and bloat-free.

Comparison Matrix: The Best Offline Android Keyboards

Keyboard App License / Source Internet Permission Gesture / Swipe Support Offline Voice Typing
HeliBoard GPL v3 (GitHub / F-Droid) No (Zero access) Yes (Via local library) Uses system speech engine
FUTO Keyboard FUTO Source-Available No (Zero access) Yes (Native on-device) Yes (Built-in offline Whisper AI)
FlorisBoard Apache 2.0 (GitHub / F-Droid) No (Zero access) Beta implementation Under active development
AnySoftKeyboard Apache 2.0 (F-Droid) No (Zero access) Yes (Basic gesture) Third-party plugin support

1. HeliBoard: The Gold Standard for Modern Android Typing

Following the stagnation of OpenBoard, the open-source community rallied behind HeliBoard, modernizing the codebase to deliver a keyboard that feels as smooth, responsive, and customizable as Gboard, but without a single byte of telemetry.

Core Features and Capabilities:

  • Familiar Material You Ergonomics: HeliBoard dynamically adapts its colors to your Android wallpaper theme, supporting dark mode, key borders, and customizable row heights.
  • Offline Glide / Gesture Typing: By loading an open-source gesture typing binary file, HeliBoard delivers lightning-fast swipe typing that rivals commercial keyboards.
  • Clipboard History Vault: Includes a local, encrypted clipboard manager that can automatically purge sensitive copied passwords after a user-defined timeout (e.g., 60 seconds).
  • Zero Network Footprint: Completely devoid of internet permissions, analytics trackers, or third-party diagnostic libraries.

How to Set Up Offline Swipe Typing in HeliBoard:

  1. Install HeliBoard from F-Droid or GitHub.
  2. Download the offline gesture library file (libjni_latinimegoogle.so) from HeliBoard's official GitHub releases repository onto your smartphone.
  3. Open HeliBoard Settings > Advanced > Load gesture typing library.
  4. Select the downloaded .so file. HeliBoard will extract the library locally into its sandboxed data partition.
  5. Enable 'Swipe typing' under Gesture typing settings. You now have fluid, accurate swipe typing completely offline!

2. FUTO Keyboard: The Cutting Edge of On-Device Voice AI

For users who rely heavily on voice dictation, migrating away from Google Voice Typing has historically been difficult because most offline speech engines produce inaccurate, robotic transcriptions. FUTO Keyboard (spearheaded by veteran programmer Louis Rossmann and the FUTO organization) completely solves this dilemma.

The Breakthrough of Local Neural Speech Models:

FUTO Keyboard packages an ultra-compact, quantized version of OpenAI's Whisper neural voice recognition model directly inside the keyboard. When you tap the microphone button:

  • Your speech audio is processed 100% on your smartphone's local NPU/CPU.
  • Transcription is shockingly fast and handles regional accents, technical jargon, and punctuation effortlessly.
  • Zero Cloud Audio Streaming: Your voice never leaves your handset. You can dictate confidential legal memos, medical notes, or personal diaries in Airplane Mode in the middle of a forest without an internet connection.

3. FlorisBoard: The Modern Kotlin Framework

Written entirely from scratch in modern Kotlin, FlorisBoard is built to be the most flexible, modular keyboard engine in the Android ecosystem. It features a stunning theme engine, rich multi-language dictionary switching, full clipboard history with pin favorites, and advanced incognito mode triggers that automatically activate whenever a browser enters private browsing mode.

Clipboard Security: Preventing Stalkerware from Scraping Passwords

Your virtual keyboard is also the primary gateway to your clipboard. When you copy a 32-character master password from Bitwarden or a banking OTP from an SMS message, standard keyboards cache that plaintext string in unencrypted memory caches. Open-source keyboards like HeliBoard and FlorisBoard implement strict clipboard defense mechanics:

  • Automated Clipboard Purging: You can configure HeliBoard to automatically overwrite and wipe copied items after 30, 60, or 120 seconds, preventing background apps from querying the clipboard buffer.
  • Incognito Mode Detection: When an app signals that it is an incognito or sensitive password field (using Android's IME_FLAG_NO_PERSONALIZED_LEARNING flag), open-source keyboards automatically disable autocomplete suggestions and refuse to store typed strings in user dictionaries.
  • Granular Dictionary Management: You can inspect, edit, or purge every single word saved in your personal dictionary with a simple text export, ensuring zero accidental storage of credit card numbers or addresses.

Why Federated Learning in Gboard and SwiftKey Is a Privacy Risk

Proponents of proprietary keyboards often claim that Google Gboard does not transmit raw keystrokes to Google servers because it utilizes Federated Learning. While technologically sophisticated, Federated Learning still exposes users to privacy leakage:

  • How Federated Learning Works: Gboard maintains a local machine learning model on your phone. When you type, the model updates its local weights to improve next-word prediction. Periodically, Gboard transmits these mathematical weight matrices (gradient updates) back to Google's central servers, where they are aggregated with millions of other users' updates.
  • The Threat of Gradient Inversion Attacks: Academic cybersecurity research has demonstrated that through 'gradient inversion attacks', a sophisticated attacker inspecting uploaded model weights can reverse-engineer the original plaintext sentences typed by individual users with up to 85% accuracy.
  • Offline Keyboards Eliminate the Math Entirely: Keyboards like HeliBoard and FUTO completely reject Federated Learning. Your text remains strictly ephemeral: when you close an app, typed data evaporates from RAM with zero model telemetry ever leaving your device.

Custom Dictionary Portability & Encrypted Backups

One fear that prevents users from leaving commercial keyboards is losing years of accumulated custom technical terms, email shortcuts, and names. HeliBoard solves this through standardized, open dictionary backups:

  1. Open HeliBoard Settings > Dictionary > Personal dictionary > Export.
  2. HeliBoard exports a clean, human-readable text file containing all your custom words and text expansion shortcuts (e.g., typing @@ expands to your full email address).
  3. You can encrypt this backup file and store it safely in your local documents or cloud backup. When setting up a new smartphone, simply tap Import to restore your entire vocabulary in three seconds without signing into a Google account.

Physical Mechanical Keyboard Support for Tablets & Foldables

As more professionals replace laptops with Android tablets (like Galaxy Tab S9 or Xiaomi Pad 6) and foldable smartphones, virtual keyboards must handle external physical hardware keyboards gracefully:

  • Hardware Keyboard Shortcuts in HeliBoard: HeliBoard includes dedicated key mapping tables for Bluetooth mechanical keyboards. You can execute standard desktop shortcuts: Ctrl + C (copy), Ctrl + V (paste), Ctrl + Z (undo), and Alt + Tab app switching.
  • Auto-Hiding the Virtual IME: When an external USB-C or Bluetooth keyboard is connected, HeliBoard automatically collapses its virtual software interface, granting you 100% of your screen estate for writing without awkward empty keyboard frames taking up space.
  • Multi-Language Hardware Switching: Pressing Ctrl + Space or Shift + Space seamlessly toggles between configured international layouts (e.g., QWERTY English, Hindi InScript, or European extended layouts) with instant visual toast notifications.

Security Checklist: Auditing Your Keyboard's Permissions

To verify that your newly installed keyboard cannot leak your keystrokes:

  1. Open Settings > Apps > All apps > [Your Keyboard].
  2. Tap Permissions.
  3. Verify that the list shows: 'No permissions allowed' (or only local storage for dictionary importing).
  4. Notice that under 'All permissions', there is no entry for 'Have full network access'. This guarantees that your keystrokes are mathematically quarantined inside your device.

Preventative Architecture & Companion Recommendations

Hardening your keyboard input closes the primary data leak on any operating system.
